newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senate urges state to sue tobacco companies.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senate urges state to sue tobacco companies.

text.p: The California state Senate called on Attorney General Dan Lungren to sue major tobacco companies for reimbursement of public health care costs incurred in treating smoking-related illnesses.

The nonbinding resolution, introduced by Democrat Sen. John Burton, was approved by the state Senate on a vote of 21-to-11 Thursday. The measure advances to the state Assembly, which could take action in the coming days.

In the last legislative session, a similar resolution was introduced and approved by the Senate but failed to clear the Republican-controlled Assembly. Since then, Democrats have taken control of the Assembly.
The resolution says California has incurred "substantial" costs treating tobacco-related diseases but does not specify the amount.
According to a recent study by the University of California, state taxpayers spent $4.1 billion in Medi-Cal expenses between 1980 and 1993 to treat smoking-related illnesses.

The attorney general's office said Lungren has looked into the possibility of a lawsuit against the tobacco companies, but has determined that it would likely fail because of a controversial state law shielding tobacco companies from product liability claims.
The law in question provides immunity from liability to a manufacturer or seller in a product liability action for certain types of consumer products.

A Senate analysis of the resolution said the law does not prohibit a lawsuit based on claims of deceptive practices by the tobacco companies since those claims cannot automatically be deemed product liability actions.
That would allow the attorney general to file a lawsuit against the tobacco industry, the Senate analysis argues.
More than 20 lawsuits have been filed by states, cities and counties against the tobacco industry aimed at recouping health care costs of smokers.
